values_verbatim: 0000–0099: Memory channel 0 to 99 | 0100: Programmed scan edge P1 | 0101: Programmed scan edge P2
visual_anchor: Memory content setting diagram under "Command: 1A 00" (PDF p.178); leftmost cell pair, indices printed as circled q, w; label in the left text column headed "q, w Memory channel number".
notes: This is the 2-byte channel selector, tier convention places it OUTSIDE the 25-byte record (as for IC-7610). Circled-numeral index font: q=1,w=2,e=3,r=4,t=5,y=6,u=7,i=8,o=9,!0=10,!1=11,!2=12,!3=13,!4=14,!5=15,!6=16,!7=17,!8=18,!9=19,@0=20…@7=27, transcribed here as plain parenthesised numbers.

visual_anchor: Memory content setting diagram (PDF p.178); single cell immediately right of the channel-number pair, index e; label "e Select memory setting".
notes: No nibble split is printed for this byte (unlike the IC-7610 record, whose corresponding byte the project's doc.go records as low-nibble select-group / high-nibble Fixed 0). Values 01/02/03 correspond to the select-memory groups ★1/★2/★3 documented elsewhere for command 0E sub-command B1/B2. High-nibble content for values 00–03 is UNVERIFIED — not stated on this page.

visual_anchor: Memory content setting diagram (PDF p.178); group bracketed r–i (indices 4–8), immediately right of the (3) cell; label "r–i Operating frequency setting / See '• Operating frequency.'". Digit table on PDF p.175 (printed p.166), under "• Operating frequency", command 00,03,05,1C 03.
notes: encoding=bcd_packed because the referenced digit table assigns each half-byte a decimal digit position of the frequency, matching the IC-7610 record's (4)-(8) group exactly in width and position.

values_verbatim: 00: LSB | 01: USB | 02: AM | 03: CW | 04: RTTY | 05: FM | 07: CW-R | 08: RTTY-R | 12: PSK | 13: PSK-R
visual_anchor: Memory content setting diagram (PDF p.178); first cell of the o, !0 pair (index 9=o); label "o, !0 Operating mode setting / See '• Operating mode.'". Code table on PDF p.175 (printed p.166), "• Operating mode", command 01, 04, 06.
notes: No 06:WFM and no 17:DV codes are printed anywhere in this table (this radio has no D-STAR) — narrower value set than IC-7610's mode enum, which includes both.

visual_anchor: Memory content setting diagram (PDF p.178); second cell of the o, !0 pair (index 10=!0), same label/cross-reference as field 9.
notes: Identical filter code set to the IC-7610 record. Page notes: "Filter setting (w) can be skipped with command 01 and 06. In that case, 'FIL1' is selected with command 01 and the default filter setting of the operating mode is selected with command 06, automatically."

values_verbatim: High nibble - Data mode: 0: OFF | 1: DATA 1 | 2: DATA 2 | 3: DATA 3 || Low nibble - Tone mode: 0: OFF | 1: TONE | 2: TSQL
visual_anchor: Memory content setting diagram (PDF p.178); single cell immediately right of the (10) cell, index !1; label "!1 Data mode setting", printed as "1 byte data (XX)" with the byte split X X and two value lists below it.
notes: encoding=enum_nibble: the page draws the byte as two X placeholders with two separate value lists, though it does not draw a dashed split rule the way the IC-7610 page does. No DTCS (3) value is printed for the tone-mode half here — the IC-7610 record's low nibble carries a fourth value, DTCS, absent on this model (no digital code squelch).

visual_anchor: Memory content setting diagram (PDF p.178); group bracketed !2–!4, immediately right of the (11) cell; label "!2–!4 Repeater tone frequency setting / See '• Repeater tone/tone squelch setting.'" No values are reprinted at the record diagram itself; the referenced digit table (PDF ~p.176-177) was not separately re-transcribed for this lane — cite is to the cross-reference line only.
notes: values_verbatim left blank: this lane did not re-open the cross-referenced tone-digit table page; width and position are taken directly from the record diagram's own bracket, matching IC-7610's (12)-(14) tone_tx group exactly.
